newsitem.title: BRAZIL: U.S.-led group buys Cemig stake for 1.13 bln reais.
newsitem.headline: U.S.-led group buys Cemig stake for 1.13 bln reais.

text.p: A consortium led by U.S.-based AES Corp and Southern Electric, a unit of Atlanta, Georgia-based Southern Company has bought a 32.96 percent voting stake in the power company Cemig for the base price of 1.13 billion reais, a bolsa official said.
The group, which also includes funds formed by local bank Opportunity, was the only bidder for debentures convertible to common shares of Cemig.
Bolsa officials said four foreign-led consortia and one local company had pre-qualified for the 0900 local/1200 GMT auction at the Rio de Janeiro Stock Exchange.
But only the AES/Southern Electric group entered a bid on the Minas Gerais state-owned firm. The gavel came down on the sale moments after the auction started.

The debentures were sold by the federal National Development Bank (BNDES), which acquired the Cemig stake late last year from Minas Gerais state, which had used the shares as collateral for a federal loan.
Minas Gerais wanted to sell the Cemig common stock in order to gain a strategic partner for the company, considered one of Brazil's most promising electrical utilities.
The BNDES had set a minimum price of 60.37 reais per lot of 1,000 shares. Analysts had said a large premium was not expected even if more than one firm entered the bidding.
The auction was originally set for late last year but was repeatedly delayed.
Late on Tuesday the state and BNDES managed to quash the last court injunctions seeking to scuttle the sale.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro Newsroom 5521 507 4151))
